records.source: וַתִּשָּׂ֨א אֹתִ֜י ר֗וּחַ וַתָּבֵ֣א אֹ֠תִי אֶל־שַׁ֨עַר בֵּית־יְהוָ֤ה הַקַּדְמוֹנִי֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ימָה וְהִנֵּה֙ בְּפֶ֣תַח הַשַּׁ֔עַר עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ וָאֶרְאֶ֨ה בְתוֹכָ֜ם אֶת־יַאֲזַנְיָ֧ה בֶן־עַזֻּ֛ר וְאֶת־פְּלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־בְּנָיָ֖הוּ שָׂרֵ֖י הָעָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And lifted me [the] Spirit and brought me to [the] gate of [the] house of Yahweh, the east [gate], that faces east; and behold, at [the] entrance of the gate twenty and five men; and I saw in their midst Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, officials of the people.
pieces: Then the Spirit lifted me up and carried me to the east gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the gate facing east. At its entrance were twenty-five men, and I saw among them Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, officials of the people.

L.1: Then the Spirit lifted me and brought me in to the gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the eastern [gate], which faces eastward; and look, at the entrance of the gate [were] twenty-five men, and I saw among them Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, officials of the people.

R.1: Then the Spirit lifted me up and took me to the east gate of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. Twenty-five men were standing at the entrance of the gate. Among them I saw two leaders of the people, Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah.

decisions.choice: the Spirit: God's Spirit, who carries the prophet in the vision (see 8:3)
alternatives: a wind
decisions.reason: See 2:2 and 8:3; in 11:24 it is called "the Spirit of God".

decisions.choice: twenty-five men, officials of the people: leaders of the city
alternatives: the same twenty-five men who bowed to the sun in 8:16
decisions.reason: These men stand at the east gate, where the glory has just stopped (10:19). The number matches 8:16, but the setting and the charge are different: these are officials who give counsel in the city (11:2). Jaazaniah son of Azzur is a different man from Jaazaniah son of Shaphan (8:11). Pelatiah's name means "the LORD rescues", and his sudden death follows in 11:13.

decisions.choice: officials (L, B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this word in the prophets: "officials" at Literal and Balanced, "leaders" at Readable.

records.heading: Twenty-five men at the east gate

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם אֵ֣לֶּה הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים הַחֹשְׁבִ֥ים אָ֛וֶן וְהַיֹּעֲצִ֥ים עֲצַת־רָ֖ע בָּעִ֥יר הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, these [are] the men who devise wickedness and who give counsel of evil in this city,
pieces: He said to me, "Son of man, these men are the ones plotting evil and giving wicked advice in this city,

L.2: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, these [are] the men, those who plan wickedness and who give evil counsel in this city,

R.2: He said to me, "Son of man, these men are planning evil and giving bad advice to the people of this city.

decisions.choice: give evil counsel: the advice of the king's officials, probably urging resistance to Babylon
decisions.reason: Officials advised the king on policy. In these years Judah's leaders were urging rebellion against Babylon with help from Egypt, against the LORD's word through Jeremiah (Jeremiah 27:9-15; 37:6-10). The text does not say what their counsel was, but their saying in 11:3 shows their false confidence.

decisions.choice: giving bad advice to the people of this city
alternatives: give evil counsel in this city
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the advice is given and ends the sentence, which in Hebrew runs on into 11:3.

records.source: הָאֹ֣מְרִ֔ים לֹ֥א בְקָר֖וֹב בְּנ֣וֹת בָּתִּ֑ים הִ֣יא הַסִּ֔יר וַאֲנַ֖חְנוּ הַבָּשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: who say, Not near [is the time for] building houses; it [is] the pot, and we [are] the meat.
pieces: who say, 'The time for building houses is not near. This city is the pot, and we are the meat.'

L.3: who say, 'Not near [is the time for] building houses; it [is] the pot, and we [are] the meat.'

R.3: They say, 'It is not the time to build houses. This city is a cooking pot, and we are the meat in it.'

decisions.choice: "not near is the building of houses": the time to build houses has not come
alternatives: a question: "Is not the time near to build houses?"
"The houses have not been built lately"
"Have not the houses been newly built?", as the Septuagint reads
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and can be read several ways. As a statement it may mean that there is no need to build, since they are safe, or it may answer Jeremiah's letter telling the exiles to build houses because their stay will be long (Jeremiah 29:5). Read as a question, it boasts that the city will soon be rebuilt. Either way it is the voice of men who think the danger is past.

decisions.choice: the city is the pot, and we are the meat: the walls protect us, and we are the choice part
decisions.reason: A cooking pot keeps the meat safe from the fire, and the meat is the valuable part, while the scraps are thrown away. The leaders mean that the city's walls protect them, and that they, not the exiles, are the true people (compare 11:15). The LORD turns the picture against them in 11:7-11, and Ezekiel uses it again in 24:3-14.

decisions.choice: a cooking pot; the meat in it
alternatives: the pot; the meat
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the pot is for cooking meat, so that the picture can be followed (m2).

records.source: לָכֵ֖ן הִנָּבֵ֣א עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם הִנָּבֵ֖א בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man.
pieces: So prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man!"

L.4: Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man!"

R.4: So prophesy against them, son of man. Prophesy!"

decisions.choice: prophesy ... prophesy: the command doubled for urgency
decisions.reason: The repeated command presses Ezekiel to speak at once.

records.source: וַתִּפֹּ֣ל עָלַי֮ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָה֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י אֱמֹר֙ כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה כֵּ֥ן אֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַעֲל֥וֹת רֽוּחֲכֶ֖ם אֲנִ֥י יְדַעְתִּֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And fell upon me [the] Spirit of Yahweh, and he said to me, Say, Thus says Yahweh: Thus you have said, house of Israel; and the things coming up [in] your spirit, I know them.
pieces: Then the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} fell on me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Say: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: That is what you are saying, house of Israel, but I know the thoughts that rise in your minds.

L.5: Then the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} fell upon me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Say, Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: So you have said, house of Israel; and the things that come up in your spirit, I know them.

R.5: Then the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told me to say, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: People of Israel, that is what you are saying. But I know what you are thinking.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of the LORD fell upon me: God's Spirit came on him to make him speak
decisions.reason: The Spirit of the LORD came on prophets to make them speak (Numbers 11:25; 1 Samuel 10:10). The verb "fell" is the one used of the LORD's hand in 8:1.

decisions.choice: the things that come up in your spirit: your thoughts and plans
decisions.reason: Here "spirit" is the human mind, as in 20:32 ("what comes up into your spirit"). The LORD knows not only what they say (11:3) but what they intend.

decisions.choice: he said to me: the speaker is the LORD, who speaks through the Spirit
alternatives: the Spirit as the speaker
decisions.reason: The one who speaks gives Ezekiel the words "Thus says the LORD", so the voice is the LORD's.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this (B); This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says (R)
alternatives: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula: "Thus says the LORD:" at Literal, "The LORD says this:" at Balanced, "This is what the LORD says:" at Readable. The message is not set in a second pair of quotation marks: the formula introduces it, as in the prophets' oracles.

records.source: הִרְבֵּיתֶ֥ם חַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וּמִלֵּאתֶ֥ם חוּצֹתֶ֖יהָ חָלָֽל׃פ
records.gloss: You have multiplied your slain in this city, and you have filled its streets [with] slain.
pieces: You have killed many people in this city and filled its streets with the dead.

L.6: You have increased your slain in this city and filled its streets [with] slain [people].

R.6: You have killed many people in this city. Its streets are full of dead bodies.

decisions.choice: your slain: those killed through your rule
alternatives: the city's war dead, for whose deaths the leaders' policies were to blame
decisions.reason: The word means people killed, usually in war. Here the leaders are said to have killed them, which points to judicial murder and violence in the city (9:9; 22:2-6, 27), though the deaths caused by their failed policies may be included.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ חַלְלֵיכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שַׂמְתֶּ֣ם בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ הֵ֥מָּה הַבָּשָׂ֖ר וְהִ֣יא הַסִּ֑יר וְאֶתְכֶ֖ם הוֹצִ֥יא מִתּוֹכָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Your slain whom you have put in its midst, they [are] the meat, and it [is] the pot; but you, bring out from its midst.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: The dead you have laid in the city are the meat, and this city is the pot; but you I will take out of it.

L.7: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Your slain whom you have laid in its midst, they [are] the meat, and this [city is] the pot; but you [I will] bring out from its midst.

R.7: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: The people you have killed and left in the city are the meat, and the city is the pot. But you will not stay in it. I will take you out.

decisions.choice: the slain are the meat and the city the pot: the only ones who stay in the "pot" are the dead
decisions.reason: The LORD takes up the leaders' saying from 11:3. The city will hold only the bodies of those they killed. The leaders themselves will not be kept safe inside it; they will be taken out to be judged (11:9-11).

decisions.choice: bring out: the verb is a bare form, read as "I will bring out"
alternatives: "he will bring you out"
"you will be brought out"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew form can be read as an infinitive used for a command or statement; many manuscripts and the ancient versions read "I will bring out", which matches 11:9.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} (L); the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this (B); this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula with "the Lord GOD", as in Isaiah and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: But you will not stay in it
alternatives: but you I will bring out
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what being taken out of the pot means for the leaders (m1).

records.source: חֶ֖רֶב יְרֵאתֶ֑ם וְחֶ֨רֶב֙ אָבִ֣יא עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: A sword you have feared, and a sword I will bring upon you, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: You fear the sword, and the sword is what I will bring against you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.8: A sword you have feared, and a sword I will bring upon you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: You are afraid of war, so I will bring war against you, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a sword: war and death in battle
decisions.reason: They trusted the city walls to keep them from the sword; what they feared will come on them.

decisions.choice: war; says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}
alternatives: the sword; declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for the sword, as the Jeremiah table does in the list "sword, famine and pestilence". "Says the Lord GOD" is the settled Readable wording for this formula.

records.source: וְהוֹצֵאתִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ מִתּוֹכָ֔הּ וְנָתַתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּיַד־זָרִ֑ים וְעָשִׂ֛יתִי בָכֶ֖ם שְׁפָטִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I will bring you out from its midst, and give you into [the] hand of foreigners, and execute against you judgments.
pieces: I will take you out of the city and hand you over to foreigners, and I will carry out judgments against you.

L.9: And I will bring you out from its midst and give you into the hand of strangers, and I will execute judgments against you.

R.9: I will take you out of the city and hand you over to foreigners, and I will punish you.

decisions.choice: foreigners: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: The foreigners are the Babylonian army, into whose hands the leaders of Jerusalem fell when the city was taken (2 Kings 25:18-21).

records.source: בַּחֶ֣רֶב תִּפֹּ֔לוּ עַל־גְּב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶשְׁפּ֣וֹט אֶתְכֶ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: By the sword you will fall; at [the] border of Israel I will judge you; and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: You will fall by the sword; I will judge you at the border of Israel. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.10: By the sword you will fall; at the border of Israel I will judge you, and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: You will be killed in war. I will punish you at the border of Israel. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: at the border of Israel: away from the city, at the edge of the land
decisions.reason: When Jerusalem fell, King Zedekiah's sons and the city's leading men were taken to the king of Babylon at Riblah, in the land of Hamath at the northern edge of Israel's land, and killed there (2 Kings 25:6-7, 18-21; Jeremiah 52:9-10, 24-27; compare Numbers 34:8). The leaders who thought the city would protect them died outside it.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD: the refrain of the book (see 6:7)
decisions.reason: See 6:7.

decisions.choice: You will be killed in war
alternatives: By the sword you will fall
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for "sword", as in 11:8.

records.source: הִ֗יא לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֤ה לָכֶם֙ לְסִ֔יר וְאַתֶּ֛ם תִּהְי֥וּ בְתוֹכָ֖הּ לְבָשָׂ֑ר אֶל־גְּב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶשְׁפֹּ֥ט אֶתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: It will not be for you a pot, and you will not be in its midst meat; at [the] border of Israel I will judge you.
pieces: This city will not be your pot, and you will not be the meat inside it. I will judge you at the border of Israel.

L.11: This [city] will not be for you a pot, and you will not be in its midst [as] meat; at the border of Israel I will judge you.

R.11: This city will not protect you as a pot protects the meat inside it. I will punish you at the border of Israel.

decisions.choice: not a pot for you, not the meat inside it: the city will not protect them
decisions.reason: The picture of 11:3 is denied outright: the city will not be their shelter.

decisions.choice: will not protect you as a pot protects the meat
alternatives: will not be a pot for you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (11:3 m2).

records.source: וִֽידַעְתֶּם֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּחֻקַּי֙ לֹ֣א הֲלַכְתֶּ֔ם וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י לֹ֣א עֲשִׂיתֶ֑ם וּֽכְמִשְׁפְּטֵ֧י הַגּוֹיִ֛ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר סְבִיבוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם עֲשִׂיתֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will know that I [am] Yahweh, in whose statutes you have not walked, and my judgments you have not done; but according to the judgments of the nations that [are] around you, you have acted.
pieces: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You have not followed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes or carried out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings; instead you have acted by the rulings of the nations around you."

L.12: And you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in whose statutes you have not walked, and whose judgments you have not done; but according to the judgments of the nations that [are] around you, you have acted."

R.12: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You did not live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws or obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules. Instead, you followed the rules of the nations around you."

decisions.choice: judgments: rulings and customs; the LORD's judgments set against those of the nations
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the LORD's judgments and for the practices of the nations. Israel was told not to live by the ways of the nations (Leviticus 18:3-4; 2 Kings 17:15). Ezekiel charges them with doing just that (5:7).

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD (see 6:7)
decisions.reason: See 6:7.

decisions.choice: statutes, judgments (L); statutes, rulings (B); laws, rules (R)
alternatives: ordinances
customs
decisions.reason: The settled wording of 5:6-7 for these two words. Each level uses the same word for the LORD's rulings and the nations', to keep the contrast.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּהִנָּ֣בְאִ֔י וּפְלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־בְּנָיָ֖ה מֵ֑ת וָאֶפֹּ֨ל עַל־פָּנַ֜י וָאֶזְעַ֣ק קוֹל־גָּד֗וֹל וָאֹמַר֙ אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה כָּלָה֙ אַתָּ֣ה עֹשֶׂ֔ה אֵ֖ת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And it was, as I prophesied, that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. And I fell on my face and cried out [with] a loud voice and said, Ah, Lord Yahweh! A full end [are] you making of [the] remnant of Israel?
pieces: While I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell face down and cried out with a loud voice, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} going to wipe out the remnant of Israel completely?"

L.13: And it came about, as I was prophesying, that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. And I fell on my face and cried out with a loud voice and said, "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} making a full end of the remnant of Israel?"

R.13: While I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. I threw myself face down on the ground and shouted, "Oh no, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} going to destroy everyone left in Israel?"

decisions.choice: Pelatiah died: his death in the vision shows the word taking effect
alternatives: an event Ezekiel learned of later, which happened in Jerusalem at the time of the vision
decisions.reason: Ezekiel is in Babylon and sees this in a vision (8:3; 11:24). The text does not say whether Pelatiah died in Jerusalem at that moment. For Ezekiel his death is a sign that the judgment he has announced is real.

decisions.choice: "Ah, Lord GOD": the cry of 9:8, asked again
decisions.reason: Ezekiel asks again whether the LORD will leave anyone (9:8). The answer comes in 11:14-21: the LORD will keep a people, among the exiles.

decisions.choice: Oh (B); Oh no (R)
alternatives: Ah
Alas
decisions.reason: As in 9:8 (following Jeremiah 1:6). Readable reuses the wording of 9:8 for the question.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.14: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me: a new word within the vision, answering Ezekiel's question
decisions.reason: The formula that begins most of Ezekiel's oracles appears here in the middle of the vision. The answer to 11:13 is that the LORD's people will survive among the exiles, not in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying: (L); came to me: (B); {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula, from the Jeremiah table. In Ezekiel, the oracle that follows it is not put in quotation marks: as in Isaiah, God's first-person speech in an oracle stands on its own, and only speech quoted within it takes quotation marks. Speech in the visions ("He said to me, ...") is quoted as narrative quotes speech.

records.heading: A sanctuary for the exiles

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם אַחֶ֤יךָ אַחֶ֨יךָ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י גְאֻלָּתֶ֔ךָ וְכָל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כֻּלֹּ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֩ אָמְר֨וּ לָהֶ֜ם יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם רַֽחֲקוּ֙ מֵעַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה לָ֥נוּ הִ֛יא נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: Son of man, your brothers, your brothers, [the] men of your redemption, and [the] whole house of Israel, all of it, [are those] of whom said [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, Go far from Yahweh; to us it [is] given, this land, as a possession.
pieces: Son of man, your brothers, your own brothers, the relatives who have the right to redeem you, and the whole house of Israel, all of them, are the ones of whom the people of Jerusalem have said, "Stay far away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! It is to us that this land has been given as a possession."

L.15: Son of man, your brothers, your brothers, the men of your redemption, and the whole house of Israel, all of it, [are those] of whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, "Go far from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; to us this land has been given as a possession."

R.15: Son of man, the people living in Jerusalem have been talking about your relatives, your own family, and about all the other people of Israel in exile. They have said, "Stay far away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! The land is ours now. It has been given to us."

decisions.choice: the men of your redemption: the relatives who had the duty to redeem a family member's land
alternatives: your fellow exiles, as the Septuagint reads
decisions.reason: Under the law the nearest relative had the right and duty to buy back a family member's land so that it stayed in the family (Leviticus 25:25), as Jeremiah did for his cousin's field (Jeremiah 32:7-8). The phrase may point to that right: those in Jerusalem were taking over the land of the exiles, who were their kin. The Septuagint reads "your fellow captives", which needs a small change in the Hebrew and fits the exiles well.

decisions.choice: "Go far from the LORD": a command, as the Hebrew is pointed
alternatives: "They have gone far from the LORD": a statement
decisions.reason: The same letters can be read as a command ("go far away") or as a statement ("they are far away"). Either way, those in Jerusalem claim that the exiles, far from the land and its temple, are far from the LORD and have lost their share in the land.

decisions.choice: "this land has been given to us as a possession": a claim to the land of the exiles
decisions.reason: The people left in Jerusalem took the exile as proof that they were the LORD's true people and heirs of the land, as Abraham was promised the land "as a possession" (Genesis 17:8; compare 33:24). The LORD answers that he is with the exiles (11:16) and will give the land to them (11:17).

decisions.choice: the people living in Jerusalem have been talking about ...; in exile
alternatives: your brothers ... of whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said
decisions.reason: Readable puts the speakers first and says who the exiles are, so that the long Hebrew sentence can be followed. It uses "relatives" and "family" for the kin who would redeem one another (m1).

records.source: לָכֵ֣ן אֱמֹ֗ר כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ כִּ֤י הִרְחַקְתִּים֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וְכִ֥י הֲפִֽיצוֹתִ֖ים בָּאֲרָצ֑וֹת וָאֱהִ֤י לָהֶם֙ לְמִקְדָּ֣שׁ מְעַ֔ט בָּאֲרָצ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁם׃ס
records.gloss: Therefore say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Though I have removed them far among the nations, and though I have scattered them among the lands, yet I have been to them a sanctuary [for a] little [while] in the lands where they have gone.
pieces: Therefore say: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Though I have sent them far off among the nations and scattered them through the lands, for a little while I have still been a sanctuary to them in the lands they have gone to.

L.16: Therefore say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Though I have removed them far off among the nations, and though I have scattered them among the lands, yet I have been to them a sanctuary for a little while in the lands where they have gone.

R.16: So tell them that this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I sent {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people far away among the nations. I scattered them in other lands. But for a while I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} have been their temple in the lands where they have gone.

decisions.choice: a sanctuary for a little while
alternatives: a sanctuary in small measure, a lesser sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word translated "a little" can mean "for a short time" or "in a small degree". On the first reading, the LORD has been the exiles' sanctuary while they are away from the temple, until he brings them back (11:17). On the second, his presence among them is real but smaller than in the temple. Later Jewish tradition applied the phrase to the synagogue.

decisions.choice: I have been to them a sanctuary: the LORD is present with the exiles, not only in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: This answers the claim of 11:15. The exiles are not far from the LORD: the LORD himself has been their holy place. Ezekiel saw the glory of the LORD in Babylon (1:1-28; 10:20), and the glory is now leaving Jerusalem (11:22-23).

decisions.choice: My people; I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}
alternatives: them
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" are and keeps the emphasis that the LORD himself was their sanctuary. It says "temple" for "sanctuary", as in 8:6.

records.source: לָכֵ֣ן אֱמֹ֗ר כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ וְקִבַּצְתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים וְאָסַפְתִּ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם מִן־הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְפֹצוֹתֶ֖ם בָּהֶ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Therefore say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: And I will gather you from the peoples, and I will assemble you from the lands where you have been scattered among them, and I will give to you [the] soil of Israel.
pieces: Therefore say: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I will gather you from the peoples and bring you together from the lands where you have been scattered, and I will give the land of Israel to you.

L.17: Therefore say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: I will gather you from the peoples and collect you from the lands in which you have been scattered, and I will give you the soil of Israel.

R.17: So tell them that this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to gather you from the nations. I will bring you back from the lands where you were scattered. Then I will give you the land of Israel.

decisions.choice: "them" becomes "you": the LORD speaks to the exiles directly
decisions.reason: In 11:16 the exiles are spoken of; here they are spoken to. The promise is addressed to the people whom those in Jerusalem had written off (11:15).

decisions.choice: the soil of Israel: the land itself, Ezekiel's usual phrase
decisions.reason: Ezekiel uses this phrase, "the ground (soil) of Israel", where other books say "the land of Israel" (7:2; 12:19). The land that those in Jerusalem claimed for themselves (11:15) will be given back to the exiles.

records.source: וּבָ֖אוּ־שָׁ֑מָּה וְהֵסִ֜ירוּ אֶת־כָּל־שִׁקּוּצֶ֛יהָ וְאֶת־כָּל־תּוֹעֲבוֹתֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: And they will come there and remove all its detestable things and all its abominations from it.
pieces: When they come there, they will remove from it all its vile idols and all its detestable practices.

L.18: And they will come there and remove from it all its detestable things and all its abominations.

R.18: When they return, they will get rid of all the disgusting idols and all the other disgusting things in the land.

decisions.choice: the returning exiles will clear the land of idols
decisions.reason: The idols and practices seen in chapter 8 will be removed by those who come back, not by those who stayed. The promise of a new heart follows at once (11:19).

decisions.choice: detestable things, abominations (L); vile idols, detestable practices (B); disgusting idols, disgusting things (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these two words in Ezekiel (see 5:9 and 5:11).

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֤י לָהֶם֙ לֵ֣ב אֶחָ֔ד וְר֥וּחַ חֲדָשָׁ֖ה אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וַהֲסִ֨רֹתִ֜י לֵ֤ב הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מִבְּשָׂרָ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לֵ֥ב בָּשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: And I will give them one heart, and a spirit new I will put within them; and I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
pieces: I will give them one heart and put a new spirit within them. I will take the heart of stone out of their bodies and give them a heart of flesh,

L.19: And I will give them one heart, and a new spirit I will put within them; and I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,

R.19: I will give them hearts that are united, and I will put a new spirit in them. I will take away their hearts that are as hard as stone and give them hearts that are tender and alive.

decisions.choice: one heart: the Hebrew text
alternatives: "another heart", as the Septuagint reads
"a new heart", as some Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac read, matching 18:31 and 36:26
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text has "one heart", an undivided heart that is loyal to the LORD alone, as in Jeremiah 32:39. The Septuagint reads "another heart", and some witnesses read "a new heart", as in 36:26; the words for "one", "another" and "new" are close in Hebrew writing. The Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: a new spirit, the heart of stone and the heart of flesh: the promise repeated in 36:26
decisions.reason: The LORD makes this promise again almost word for word in 36:26-27, where he adds "I will put my Spirit within you". In 18:31 Israel is told to make itself "a new heart and a new spirit". Paul uses the picture of hearts of flesh in 2 Corinthians 3:3.

decisions.choice: heart and spirit: the mind and will; stone and flesh: hardness and responsiveness
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is the seat of thought and decision as well as feeling. A heart of stone is one that cannot respond to God (compare Zechariah 7:12); a heart of flesh is alive and able to respond. "Spirit" here is the people's inner life, written with a small letter; in 36:27 the LORD speaks of "my Spirit".

decisions.choice: hearts that are united; hearts that are as hard as stone; hearts that are tender and alive
alternatives: one heart; the heart of stone; a heart of flesh
decisions.reason: Readable explains the pictures (m3). It uses the plural "hearts" because it speaks of the people one by one.

records.source: לְמַ֨עַן֙ בְּחֻקֹּתַ֣י יֵלֵ֔כוּ וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֥י יִשְׁמְר֖וּ וְעָשׂ֣וּ אֹתָ֑ם וְהָיוּ־לִ֣י לְעָ֔ם וַאֲנִ֕י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: so that in my statutes they may walk, and my judgments they may keep and do them; and they will be to me a people, and I will be to them God.
pieces: so that they will follow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and carefully carry out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings. They will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.

L.20: so that in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes they may walk, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments they may keep and do them; and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.

R.20: Then they will live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and carefully obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules. They will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.

decisions.choice: they will be my people, and I will be their God: the words of the covenant
decisions.reason: This is the central promise of the covenant (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12; Jeremiah 24:7; 31:33). Ezekiel repeats it in 14:11; 36:28 and 37:23, 27.

decisions.choice: so that they may walk in my statutes: the new heart makes obedience possible
decisions.reason: In 11:12 the people had not walked in the LORD's statutes. The new heart and spirit are given so that they will.

records.source: וְאֶל־לֵ֧ב שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֛ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֣ם הֹלֵ֑ךְ דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: But to [the] heart of their detestable things and their abominations their heart goes; their way on their heads I will put, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: But as for those whose hearts are devoted to their vile idols and detestable practices, I will bring their conduct down on their own heads, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: But [as for those whose] heart goes to the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, their way I will bring down on their heads, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: But some people's hearts are set on their disgusting idols and disgusting practices. I will pay them back for what they have done, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: whose heart goes after the heart of their detestable things: those devoted to their idols
alternatives: "whose heart goes after their detestable things", if one "heart" is a copying error
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is awkward: "to the heart of their detestable things ... their heart goes". It may mean that their heart follows the idols' "heart", what the idols want, or the doubled word may be a scribal slip. The sense is clear: these are the people who will not turn from their idols.

decisions.choice: I will bring their way on their heads: as 9:10
decisions.reason: See 9:10. The promise of 11:17-20 is not for those who hold on to their idols.

records.source: וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ הַכְּרוּבִים֙ אֶת־כַּנְפֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָאֽוֹפַנִּ֖ים לְעֻמָּתָ֑ם וּכְב֧וֹד אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִלְמָֽעְלָה׃
records.gloss: And lifted the cherubim their wings, and the wheels alongside them; and [the] glory of [the] God of Israel [was] over them from above.
pieces: Then the cherubim spread their wings, with the wheels beside them, while the glory of the God of Israel was above them.

L.22: Then the cherubim lifted up their wings, with the wheels alongside them, and the glory of the God of Israel [was] upon them from above.

R.22: Then the cherubim spread their wings, and the wheels went with them. The glory of the God of Israel was above them.

decisions.choice: the cherubim lifted their wings: the scene of 10:19 resumes
decisions.reason: The narrative returns to the throne waiting at the east gate (10:19) and tells its last move.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַל֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל תּ֣וֹךְ הָעִ֑יר וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ עַל־הָהָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִקֶּ֥דֶם לָעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And went up [the] glory of Yahweh from over [the] midst of the city and stood on the mountain that [is] east of the city.
pieces: The glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went up from the middle of the city and stopped over the mountain east of the city.

L.23: And the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went up from over the midst of the city and stood on the mountain that [is] east of the city.

R.23: The glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rose up and left the city. It stopped over the hill east of the city.

decisions.choice: the mountain east of the city: the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: The ridge east of Jerusalem, across the Kidron Valley, is the Mount of Olives (2 Samuel 15:30; Zechariah 14:4). The text does not name it.

decisions.choice: the glory leaves the city: the last stage of its departure
decisions.reason: The glory has moved from the most holy place to the threshold (9:3; 10:4), to the east gate (10:18-19), and now out of the city. Without the LORD's presence, the temple and the city in which the leaders trusted are left to judgment. In 43:1-5 Ezekiel sees the glory return from the east.

records.source: וְר֣וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֗תְנִי וַתְּבִיאֵ֤נִי כַשְׂדִּ֨ימָה֙ אֶל־הַגּוֹלָ֔ה בַּמַּרְאֶ֖ה בְּר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֨עַל֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִֽיתִי׃
records.gloss: And [the] Spirit lifted me and brought me to Chaldea, to the exiles, in the vision, by [the] Spirit of God; and went up from me the vision that I had seen.
pieces: Then the Spirit lifted me up and, in the vision given by the Spirit of God, brought me back to the exiles in Chaldea. And the vision I had seen left me.

L.24: And the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to Chaldea, to the exiles, in the vision, by the Spirit of God; and the vision that I had seen went up from me.

R.24: Then in the vision, God's Spirit lifted me up and brought me back to the exiles in Babylonia. Then the vision I had seen ended.

decisions.choice: the Spirit brought me back: the end of the journey begun in 8:3
decisions.reason: The vision began when the Spirit lifted Ezekiel and brought him to Jerusalem "in visions of God" (8:3). Now the Spirit brings him back to Chaldea, that is, Babylonia, where he had been sitting with the elders (8:1).

decisions.choice: Babylonia
alternatives: Chaldea
decisions.reason: Readable says "Babylonia" for the land of the Chaldeans, as it says "Babylonians" for the Chaldeans.

records.source: וָאֲדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־הַגּוֹלָ֑ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶרְאָֽנִי׃פ
records.gloss: And I spoke to the exiles all [the] things of Yahweh that he had shown me.
pieces: And I told the exiles everything that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had shown me.

L.25: And I spoke to the exiles all the things of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had shown me.

R.25: Then I told the exiles everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had shown me.

decisions.choice: I told the exiles: the elders of 8:1 hear the vision
decisions.reason: The vision was given while the elders of Judah sat before Ezekiel (8:1). Its message is for the exiles: the LORD has left the temple of Jerusalem, and his future for his people lies with them.
